reasons: The cited paragraph (Section 7.5(b)) is accurately quoted and does expressly negate any licence of the Servicer's processes, models and servicing software to a Successor Servicer or third party, with no mechanism to add the Issuer, its Affiliates or its contractors — this matches the rule's walk-away description ('affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them'), so a deviation classification (rather than compliant/fallback) is correct and is not over-flagging.
Direction is right for our side: the restriction operates against the Issuer/Depositor (our party) and the Servicer/Cellco is the counterparty, so this is not a clause that benefits us.

The redline is actionable and reaches the playbook preferred position on all material terms: non-exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free grant, extended to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (including any Successor Servicer), and transferable to successors; it is scoped to what is necessary to service the Receivables and preserves the genuine legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection carve-outs, so it is not gratuitously broad.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.603 changed-character ratio) is justified here: the original sentence is an outright disclaimer of any licence, so it cannot be brought to the playbook position without replacing it with an affirmative grant.

Comment is accurate, appropriately prefixed, first-person plural and concise; it states what changed, why (servicing continuity on transfer) and that carve-outs were preserved. Minor, non-disqualifying points: narrowing the pre-existing transfer/confidentiality carve-out to restrictions 'in favor of an unaffiliated third party' goes slightly beyond the minimum needed, and because 'Servicer' is defined to include a Successor Servicer the grant language is mildly circular — both are drafting refinements rather than substantive defects, and the fallback (affiliates on notice, successor transfer) could be offered in negotiation.
